title: Two-line Weyl product classification and Fourier-hard factor theorem
main_results: For two independent Weyl directions, the dephased Fourier coefficient tensor has rank 1 when kappa=0 and rank N otherwise.
All compatible ordered pairs are v=t(a-b,a+b) with a^2+b^2 nonzero.
Every compatible pair gives an exact quadratic-chirp line factorization of the Fourier matrix.
Every nonvertical compatible line factor is diagonally/permutationally Fourier-equivalent; a vertical factor is diagonal.
An incompatible fixed pair needs at least N product terms in any sum-of-products representation.
A local rational/Green realization of a hard factor needs denominator degree at least floor((N-e)/2).
status: No exact sub-NlogN FFT; the two-line product route is classified and yields no simplification.
